title: 🎙️ Gemini speaks in 66 new voices... and 'Notebook' turns your notes into an interactive website!
body: 🎙️ Gemini speaks in 66 new voices... and 'Notebook' turns your notes into an interactive website!

Google has added two new updates to its 'Gemini' assistant: the first is 66 new regional voices in the Gemini app on Android and iPhone, including American, British, and Indian English, Hindi, Brazilian Portuguese, Indonesian, and Korean. Google says these voices reflect local speech patterns in rhythm and pitch, not exaggerated accents, and you can preview and choose them from the three-dot menu in 'Gemini Live' or from the voice settings, and the voice you choose will be used throughout the app, including live voice conversations, language-learning exercises, and read-aloud replies.

The second update concerns 'Gemini Notebook': you can now turn the materials saved in your notebook into an interactive website, simply by writing 'make me a website' in the conversation and describing what you want. For example, study material can become an interactive periodic table or a historical timeline, sales figures a tracking dashboard, or tasks a deadline and task tracker. The feature is available now worldwide on the web for users aged 18 and over and for 'Google Workspace' subscribers, with phone app support coming later.
Simply put: imagine your smart assistant now speaking in a voice like the people of your country, and your scattered notes turning with one tap into a beautiful website you can browse and share.
Which update matters more to you: the new voices, or turning notes into a website?
